# Tokenization Systems

> Independent research, advisory, and infrastructure practice on digital money, tokenization, and tokenomics. Nine SSRN working papers and 25 federal comment letters across the GENIUS Act and related dockets, the first eight filed across a 10-day window in April 2026. Run by Zach Zukowski (six years as Senior Investment Analyst at Borderless Capital).

Site: https://tokenization.systems
Contact: zach@tokenization.systems

## About

- [About Tokenization Systems](https://tokenization.systems/about/): what the practice is, what it publishes, who runs it, how to cite it, and the licence terms.

## Research

- [All research](https://tokenization.systems/research/): Nine-paper program across Track A (stablecoins, gateways, settlement infrastructure) and Track B (tokenomics, DePIN, protocol-network governance).
- [Routing the Dollar](https://tokenization.systems/papers/routing-the-dollar/): Stablecoin stress performance varies by gateway, not by token. Three descriptive findings from on-chain data, February 2023 through January 2026 (SSRN 6267698). Prepared for FRBNY's Fifth Conference on International Roles of the U.S. Dollar (June 2026).
- [Minimum Viable Equivalence Pack (MVEP)](https://tokenization.systems/papers/mvep/): Ten-category committee checklist testing whether a tokenized product maintains equivalence under stress. Reverse-engineered from the SVB weekend (SSRN 6363138).
- [Seven Dollars](https://tokenization.systems/papers/seven-dollars/): Comparative framework for seven major dollar-denominated digital products across a five-marker design scorecard (SSRN 6483118).
- [Three Tokenization Strategies](https://tokenization.systems/papers/three-strategies/): Institutional tokenization is proceeding through three distinct strategies: regulated collateral, multi-issuer yield stack, and tokenized equity on Nasdaq and NYSE; Securitize is transfer agent in all three (SSRN 6483198).
- [Who Controls Agentic Payments?](https://tokenization.systems/papers/who-controls-agentic-payments/): First control-layer measurement of agentic payments across x402 on Base, Solana, and Polygon; facilitator concentration clears merger-guidelines thresholds on every chain, and the count layer and value layer have different monopolists (SSRN 7396241).
- [Adaptive Tokenomics](https://tokenization.systems/papers/adaptive-tokenomics/): Systems-engineering approach to programmable incentive design; PID-controlled adaptive emissions compress worst-case variance 6x across 240 Monte Carlo simulations (SSRN 6364158).
- [Operational Risk in Token Economies](https://tokenization.systems/papers/operational-risk/): 624-configuration, 1,126-run simulation battery testing how infrastructure failures interact with adaptive controllers and reputation-weighted governance (SSRN 6352118).
- [Who Burns the Tokens?](https://tokenization.systems/papers/who-burns-the-tokens/): Fiscal sustainability and demand concentration in GeoDePIN networks across Helium, GEODNET, Hivemapper, and Livepeer (SSRN 6483619).
- [Governance Concentration Beyond Token Allocation](https://tokenization.systems/papers/governance-concentration/): Live-governance audit of 52 token protocols published in Frontiers in Blockchain (Blockchain Economics, August 2026; 9:1853465, doi 10.3389/fbloc.2026.1853465; SSRN 6599278).

## Frameworks

- [Frameworks](https://tokenization.systems/frameworks/): Diligence frameworks the program publishes.
- Control Layer Intensity Index (CLII): five-dimension regulatory-posture score for stablecoin gateways.
- Minimum Viable Equivalence Pack (MVEP): ten-category diligence framework for institutional tokenization.
- MVEP-AI: ten-category framework adapted for AI-operator diligence (composed-product, foundation-model, agentic systems).
- CLII-AI: five-dimension regulatory-posture score for AI operators (Tier 1/2/3 placement).
- FQPSI / PPSI: federal payment-stablecoin issuer diligence frameworks.

## Federal comment letters

- [All letters](https://tokenization.systems/letters/): 25 federal comment letters across nineteen dockets to nine federal agencies, from the GENIUS Act implementation cycle and the SEC draft strategic plan to the CFTC clearing-organization collection, Treasury's section 3 issuance proposal, and the SEC's Regulation Crypto Assets proposal and tokenized NMS stock exemptions. Filed April 10 to October 19, 2026.
- Covers OCC bank stablecoin engagement, Treasury GENIUS Act state similarity and section 3 issuance, FDIC payment-stablecoin reserve standards, subsidiary-issuance approvals, resolution submissions, assessments, and disclosure of supervisory information, FinCEN AML/CFT and Permitted Payment Stablecoin Issuer (PPSI) sanctions and customer identification, joint banking AML/CFT, the Board of Governors AML program rule, the SEC draft strategic plan, Regulation Crypto Assets, and tokenized NMS stock exemptions, and the CFTC clearing-organization information collection.

- [Recommendation index](https://tokenization.systems/letters/recommendations/): 136 numbered recommendations across the letters in one table, by letter, agency and topic, with the status of each as final rules issue.
- [Outcomes so far](https://tokenization.systems/letters/#program-outcomes): one row per proceeding with the comment-period close, the status of the final rule and next dates; also available as an Atom feed at https://tokenization.systems/letters/feed.xml.
- [GENIUS Act rulemaking tracker](https://tokenization.systems/trackers/genius-act/): every implementing rulemaking under the GENIUS Act with publication date, comment deadline, status and sources, including the ones the program did not comment on; also published as JSON at https://tokenization.systems/trackers/genius-act/genius-act.json.

## Notes

- [Notes](https://tokenization.systems/notes/): short, dated notes on rulemaking status, market events and equivalence checks, with an Atom feed at https://tokenization.systems/notes/feed.xml.

## Data and code

- [Data and code](https://tokenization.systems/data/): the letters registry as JSON and CSV, the GENIUS Act tracker as JSON, the compiled letters PDF, and each paper's replication repository, with licences (research content CC BY 4.0).

## Research infrastructure

A cited-research system architecture underlies the program: hundreds of academic sources in a graph-indexed substrate with nine AI-integration patterns for paper drafting, synthesis, revision-impact analysis, cluster discovery, bibliography generation, cross-paper claim synthesis, verbatim quote retrieval, author cluster discovery, and reverse-index lookup. The program's multi-agent research infrastructure, including the Canonical-State Architecture for multi-session coordination, is patent-pending, with 41 filed USPTO applications across 31 families spanning concurrent repository integrity, evidence and retrieval quality, provenance and artifact coherence, coordination, fleet governance, and session continuity, measurement and detector validity, and on-chain governance and control attribution; the methodology paper documenting the substrate is in development.

- [Patent-Pending Systems](https://tokenization.systems/patents/): 41 filed USPTO applications across 31 families, grouped into six problem areas with USPTO application numbers.

## Engagement and contact

- [Field guide (Start Here)](https://tokenization.systems/overview/): Definitions, four dollar objects, five diagnostic questions, and the six-step decision map for evaluating tokenized financial products.
- [Agent infrastructure](https://tokenization.systems/agent-infrastructure/): Empirical control-layer governance and safeguards for concurrent multi-agent fleets.
- [Advisory and speaking](https://tokenization.systems/speaker-and-advisory/): Talks, workshops, and advisory engagements on digital-money infrastructure, tokenization diligence, and token-economy design.
- [Contact](https://tokenization.systems/contact/): Direct contact for advisory, speaking, and research-collaboration inquiries.

## Resume profiles

- [Asset management](https://tokenization.systems/resume/asset-management/): Research, diligence, and decision frameworks for tokenized products and institutional capital allocation.
- [Policy and central banking](https://tokenization.systems/resume/policy/): Research on digital money, stablecoins, settlement, and control-layer infrastructure for policy and market-infrastructure roles.
- [AI governance and infrastructure](https://tokenization.systems/resume/ai-governance-infrastructure/): AI-operator diligence and accountability frameworks (MVEP-AI, CLII-AI).
- [Risk and controls](https://tokenization.systems/resume/risk-controls/): Stress scenarios, finality, and operational risk for tokenized products.
- [Product](https://tokenization.systems/resume/product/): Product strategy for digital-money and tokenized-asset platforms.
- [Stablecoin and payments](https://tokenization.systems/resume/stablecoin-payments/): Gateway routing, reserve mechanics, and payment-stablecoin operator diligence.
